newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium smelter capacity seen up 717,000 T in 97.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium smelter capacity seen up 717,000 T in 97.

text.p: Western aluminium smelter capacity is expected to increase by 717,000 tonnes by the end of the year, more than twice the rise in 1996, broker Billiton Metals said in a report.
"It is clear that Western production this year this year will be higher than we believed at the start of the year," the report said.
"More significantly perhaps, production during the second half of the year will be substantially higher than in the first six months," it added.
Smelter capacity rose by 338,000 tonnes last year.

Even if demand in the second half is as strong as the first half -- which is uncertain considering the restocking which has taken place -- the market is likely to move from deficit to a fairly small surplus as the year progresses.
The largest single addition to capacity is expected in Australia with Comalco Ltd's Boyne Island smelter, which will probably be completed by August, six months ahead of schedule.
The expansion will probably exceed its design capacity of 217,000 tonnes and may be capable of producing as much as 230,000 tonnes, Billiton said.
The second biggest increase is in Dubai, where Dubai Aluminium completed its 140,000 tonne expansion eight weeks ahead of schedule in January.
In New Zealand, Comalco's Tiwai Point smelter is expected to reach full capacity of 313,000 tonnes by mid-year, following a 43,000 tonne uptrade.
The expansion of the Straumsvik smelter in Iceland from 100,000 to 162,000 tonnes per year is seen starting up in July. It is owned by Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG.
